text:
Viggo Björck was drafted eighth overall in June and is already a regular for Winnipeg at 18, playing 14 minutes a night. He scored his first NHL goal against Ottawa last week, and The Athletic's Jesse Granger described it as "incredible hands." Sportsnaut wrote that he and Cole Perfetti give Jets fans a glimpse of the future.

The numbers are better than his six points in 24 games suggest. Winnipeg takes 56% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances), 11 points better than without him, on a team that is under water overall. He also has two goals on 3.9 expected, and the Jets have scored about 3.4 fewer goals than their chances with him on the ice, so the points should come. For context, of the 55 forwards picked sixth to tenth from 2005 to 2024 with four-plus seasons, 48 reached 200 NHL games. He had 15 points as a teenager in the SHL last season. Our range has him around 27 points by April. An 18-year-old tilting the ice is the best news the Jets have had in a while.
